newsitem.title: CHINA: China executes 38 more drug traffickers.
newsitem.headline: China executes 38 more drug traffickers.

text.p: China got tough on drug dealers on Thursday, executing at least 38 people just a day after 27 others were shot by firing squad in a key southwestern narcotics trafficking region.

Authorities in the southwestern province of Sichuan ordered the immediate executions of 24 drug dealers after announcing their sentences at a mass rally in the provincial capital, Sichuan, the official Xinhua news agency said.
City authorities destroyed 10 kg of drugs, it said.
Authorities in the city passed sentence on 90 people convicted of drugs-related crime, of whom 24 were executed and 16 given the death penalty with a two-year reprieve.
The Beijing Number One People's Court sentenced 14 people to death on Thursday and ordered their immediate execution. Authorities destroyed 20 kg of drugs, Xinhua said.
China routinely executes drug traffickers to try to crack down on smuggling and addiction that have proliferated in recent years.
The southeastern province of Fujian announced it had arrested 569 suspected drug traffickers and confiscated more than 320 kg of drugs in the first five months of the year.

China executed 27 drug traffickers and burnt one tonne of heroin on Wednesday in its battle against drugs in southwestern Yunnan province that borders the notorious drug-producing region formed in the Golden Triangle of Vietnam, Laos and Burma.
Beijing's authoritarian communist rulers virtually eradicated drugs in China, where opium addiction was rampant in the 19th and early 20th centuries, after they swept to power in 1949.
